# Atum Drive engine protocol 1.1

Status: S4-3 contract checkpoint for the approved [Drive plan](../plans/2026-10-06-codex-4-drive.md), sections 6.6 and 7. This checkpoint contains data and documentation only. It does not activate engine features or change the desktop bridge. S4-6 implements the app; S4-8/S4-9 implement the engine after this checkpoint merges.

The source of truth is `atum-platform/atum-app`. Both endpoints are bundled in one signed app; the engine manifest continues to say `protocol: 1`. The app checks the executable and entire bundle SHA-256 before launch. The engine repository vendors these fixtures byte for byte using the digest recipe below. A new contract revision must retain the 1.0 compatibility cases.

## Transport and validation

Each direction is UTF-8 JSON objects, one compact object followed by LF per frame. Maximum **16,384 UTF-8 bytes including LF** (16,383 bytes of JSON). The cap applies to each frame and the pending incomplete line, not a whole OS read containing several lines. Test receivers with both fragmented frames and several frames in one read. CRLF, invalid UTF-8, blank lines, malformed JSON and non-objects are rejected. Senders emit each object key once; receivers use their existing JSON decoder rather than adding a second lexical parser. Diagnostics go to stderr; stdout contains only protocol frames. Neither side logs raw payloads or includes them in exceptions.

All new frame schemas below have exactly the stated required keys and optional keys: unknown keys, wrong types, unknown enum values or a wrong direction fail closed. `N` below means an integer in `0..9007199254740991`; booleans are not integers. Bytes, counts, timestamps and ETA cannot be negative, fractional, non-finite or unsafe for the JavaScript endpoint. Times are epoch milliseconds in UTC. A display time is localized by the renderer.

`handle` means an opaque string matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`. It must not encode a local path, DAV href, subject, token or remote resource ID. Engine-owned item handles and cursors are random references into an engine-private map, scoped to that process, owner and root. They expire on process exit, owner change, disconnect or root change. Request IDs are generated by the requesting app, unique while pending, and echoed exactly once. Only the expected reply kind may complete a request.

The existing 1.0 frames (`hello`, `start`, `authorize`, `state`, `file_metadata`, `stop`, `forget`, `cleanup`) keep their existing semantics and guards. In particular, the `start` frame still carries native `root` and `configDir` **only between main and engine**; file-metadata capability grants stay main-owned and do not become presentation facts. This contract does not redefine those schemas beyond the additive handshake. Legacy validation must not be accidentally tightened by a new-frame parser.

## Two-way feature handshake

The engine emits one `hello` before any other frame:

```json
{"kind":"hello","protocol":1,"origin":"https://drive.atum.test","issuer":"https://auth.atum.test/","taskFiles":true,"features":["progress","sync","quota","trash","exclusions"]}
```

The identity fields must match main's pinned engine/owner identity using the existing comparison. `taskFiles` remains independent of the new features. `features` is optional; absent means an engine speaking 1.0. When present it is a unique array of at most eight entries from the closed set `progress`, `sync`, `quota`, `trash`, `exclusions`. Empty is valid. A protocol other than 1, an unknown or duplicate feature, or a second hello is a protocol failure.

Main sends its existing `start` plus the subset it accepts:

```json
{"kind":"start","issuer":"https://auth.atum.test/","subject":"synthetic-owner","root":"/tmp/atum-synthetic/Drive","configDir":"/tmp/atum-synthetic/engine","features":["progress","sync","quota"]}
```

Every accepted feature must have been offered. An absent `start.features` means an old app accepting **none**. Main omits `features` entirely when the engine's hello omitted it, preserving the exact legacy start shape. An engine advertising features and receiving the legacy start runs the legacy protocol. Features are negotiated once per child, never changed while connected.

**The engine never sends what the app did not accept.** Each new frame is fenced by its matching feature. Main never sends `trash_list` or `trash_restore` without `trash`. An offered but unaccepted feature is insufficient. Reject a gated frame arriving before start, without acceptance, in the wrong direction or with an unknown kind. Negotiation does not add model tools or alter a conversation's prompt/toolset.

| Feature | Engine → main | Main → engine |
| --- | --- | --- |
| progress | `progress` | — |
| sync | `sync` | — |
| quota | `quota` | — |
| trash | `trash`, `trash_result` | `trash_list`, `trash_restore` |
| exclusions | `exclusions` | — |

## Progress, sync and quota

### `progress`

```json
{"kind":"progress","active":true,"files":{"done":12,"total":40},"bytes":{"done":3000000,"total":10000000},"etaSeconds":60,"direction":"mixed"}
```

Required keys: `kind`, `active` (boolean), `files`, `bytes`, `etaSeconds` (`N` or null), `direction` (`up`, `down`, `mixed`). Each counter object has exactly `done:N,total:N`, with done ≤ total. Null ETA means no reliable estimate. Zero counters are valid for an empty run.

Within one active run, both done counters and both totals cannot decrease. An `active:false` frame terminates the run and carries its final nondecreasing counters; it does **not** imply done = total or a successful sync. The next `active:true` begins a new run and may reset counters. No names, paths or current-file labels are carried. The engine emits snapshots at least 500 ms apart (at most two per second), including the terminal snapshot; a terminal snapshot waits at most 500 ms behind the preceding snapshot. Main publishes progress at most once per 500 ms; state/error transitions retain their existing timely publication. Emission rate is a sender obligation tested against the engine, **not** an arrival-time rejection rule: OS buffering can deliver compliant snapshots in one read. Main coalesces such bursts.

### `sync`

```json
{"kind":"sync","lastSyncAt":1791281400000,"conflicts":1,"errors":0,"excluded":3}
```

Required keys: `kind`, `lastSyncAt:N`, `conflicts:N`, `errors:N`, `excluded:N`. Emit after each completed run. `lastSyncAt` is the last successful sync time from the engine's SyncResult, never main's receipt time. Zero means never successfully synced and is not displayed as a date. A failed run preserves the previous successful timestamp; that timestamp cannot regress within a process. Counts describe the completed run, not a lifetime total. No file names, paths, remote IDs or error strings are carried.

Main derives `conflicts` and `errors` issue codes from these counts. A nonzero generic errors count does not identify HTTP 507 or promise seven-day retention. Drive-full status comes from the quota fact or a separately confirmed broker `drive_full` outcome. The plan's future 507-specific classification must have explicit engine evidence; these aggregate counts alone cannot supply it.

### `quota`

```json
{"kind":"quota","total":1073741824,"used":300000000,"remaining":773741824,"state":"normal"}
```

Required keys: `kind`, `total:N`, `used:N`, `remaining:N`, `state` (`normal`, `nearing`, `critical`, `exceeded`). Total must be positive. `remaining = max(total - used, 0)`; used may exceed total. `exceeded` means used ≥ total and remaining = 0; the other states require used < total. Threshold choices for nearing/critical remain the existing spaces-manager policy, not a new timer or network query in main.

The engine forwards its spaces manager's own drive quota on refresh and once after enrolment. **No new Graph request or polling timer.** An unavailable/unlimited/invalid quota does not produce a fabricated zero-usage frame. The view omits quota until a valid fact exists; Add to Drive may separately use the plan's clearly labelled local estimate. The quota stays 1 GiB; this contract grants no quota change.

## Trash listing and restore

### `trash_list` and `trash`

First-page request (required keys `kind`, `requestId:handle`):

```json
{"kind":"trash_list","requestId":"list-1"}
```

Subsequent page adds optional `after:handle`, from that process's previous `next`:

```json
{"kind":"trash_list","requestId":"list-2","after":"cursor-1"}
```

Reply (required `kind`, `requestId:handle`, `items`; optional `next:handle`):

```json
{"kind":"trash","requestId":"list-1","items":[{"id":"item-1","name":"report.pdf","deletedAt":1791280800000,"size":4096,"type":"file"}],"next":"cursor-1"}
```

Items contain exactly `id:handle`, `name`, `deletedAt:N`, `size:N`, `type` (`file`, `folder`). Names are display basenames: nonempty, at most 255 UTF-8 bytes, not `.` or `..`, no slash, backslash, NUL or control character. They are the only human file names added by 1.1 and reach only the Recently deleted view; never diagnostics. Their bytes are never interpreted as a path by main or renderer. Engine-private DAV metadata resolves the opaque item ID.

At most **40 items per frame**, unique IDs, newest deletion first (ties ordered consistently by opaque ID across that listing). The encoded byte cap takes priority: an engine may return fewer than 40. A nonterminal page is nonempty and has `next`; the cursor must advance. Omitted `next` means complete; an empty items array without next is a proven empty final page. The engine accesses only the enrolled owner's personal space through the ingress's trash-bin routes using its own token. A DAV/auth/network/parser failure must never be reported as an empty listing: use the existing appropriate `state` failure/offline/reauthenticate transition, fail the pending operation, and preserve the previous UI list as stale.

An invalid/expired cursor fails the operation through the existing error state; it never selects another space or silently restarts a listing. Main serializes list/restore operations for the active child and cancels them on state loss/disconnect. Replies must match an outstanding request, correct kind, current child generation and owner/root; replies from a retired child are discarded before dispatch. Duplicate or mismatched replies from the current child fail protocol validation.

### `trash_restore` and `trash_result`

Request (required keys only):

```json
{"kind":"trash_restore","requestId":"restore-1","id":"item-1"}
```

Reply (required keys only):

```json
{"kind":"trash_result","requestId":"restore-1","id":"item-1","result":"restored"}
```

`requestId` and `id` are handles. The result set is closed:

| Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| restored | Server confirmed restoration to the original name. |
| renamed | Server confirmed restoration with a suffix because the original name exists. |
| not_found | Item vanished/expired or the handle is not in this process's owner/root map. No write attempted for an unknown handle. |
| no_room | Server definitively refused for quota/507 (`drive_full`); no successful restore. |
| failed | Other failure or ambiguous result; no automatic restore retry. Refresh the list before a new owner action. |

Restore never overwrites or replaces an existing file. The engine chooses keep-both behavior server-side; no delete-and-replace sequence is allowed. The engine does not translate a handle into a path chosen by main. Main receives neither the token, remote ID nor restored path. On successful restoration the old handle is invalidated and the app refreshes listing/quota. A repeated owner request for that old handle returns not_found without a second write. No permanent-delete command is added. Retention remains **168 hours**; a seven-day retention sentence is not a guarantee that every missing/failed item can be recovered.

## Exclusions

```json
{"kind":"exclusions","patterns":["token",".env",".git","node_modules"]}
```

Required keys only: `kind`, `patterns` (unique array of 1..256 nonempty glob strings, each ≤256 UTF-8 bytes). The line must fit the byte cap; never truncate an authoritative list. Patterns are relative exclusion expressions, not paths or executable regular expressions: no absolute/drive-letter path, NUL/control character or `..` path segment. Forward the engine's actual exclusion list, including its credential/tool-folder additions; do not maintain a second handwritten list. If the full list cannot fit, do not advertise `exclusions` and keep the app's pinned snapshot. The four names in the example are minimum promised exclusions, not the complete upstream list.

## Compatibility, errors and UI authority

| Pair | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| 1.0 engine + new app | Hello has no features; app sends unchanged legacy start and receives legacy frames. Existing Drive screen remains usable. |
| New engine + old app | Hello offers features; absent start.features accepts none. Engine emits only legacy frames. |
| Both new, partial subset | Only accepted facts/commands are emitted; unsupported UI actions are unavailable. |
| New frame without opt-in, unknown kind, wrong direction, malformed field, over-cap line, counter regression | Fail closed as `protocol`; terminate that connection using existing recovery. Do not touch files, change root, forget credentials or pretend the operation succeeded. |
| Server offline/auth failure | Existing state/recovery path; retain prior presentation facts only as stale. Never infer sync from folder existence. |

Main owns native paths and capability handles; the renderer receives typed presentation facts. Additive view fields and bridge methods are S4-5/S4-6/S4-7, not new engine wire kinds. Issues stay the view's closed codes (`drive_full`, `conflicts`, `errors`, `signed_out`) with opaque row IDs. Do not invent an `issues` engine frame. State stays authoritative from the engine heartbeat. The engine's sync time supersedes the interim 0.18.3 main-clock field when available.

## Fixture format and pin

Fixtures live at `apps/desktop/electron/matrix/__fixtures__/drive-engine-1.1/`. Each JSONL row is one test envelope, **not a wire frame**:

```json
{"id":"quota-normal","direction":"engine_to_app","context":{"phase":"started","offered":["quota"],"accepted":["quota"]},"wire":"{\"kind\":\"quota\",\"total\":1073741824,\"used\":300000000,\"remaining\":773741824,\"state\":\"normal\"}\n","expected":{"verdict":"accept","code":"ok"}}
```

Pass the decoded `wire` string's UTF-8 bytes to the real receiver, not the envelope serialization. Every row has an expected verdict. `context` initializes the preceding handshake, identity, active counters, last timestamp and/or pending request; it is test data, never accepted from the engine. Optional `chunks` are byte lengths splitting that same wire; omitted means one write. A wire may include consecutive frames to prove OS-read independence. Reject rows report contract reason codes for fixtures only; production still exposes the existing sanitized `protocol` failure.

`vendored.json` records individual SHA-256 digests plus a pack digest. Compute the pack digest by sorting the **contract doc plus all `.jsonl` files** by their repository-relative ASCII paths and hashing, for each, compact JSON `[path,sha256]` followed by LF. Hash raw file bytes, including final LF. The pin file excludes itself. An engine vendor record names the merged app source SHA and this pack digest; no circular self-SHA or claim that an unmerged commit was vendored. Consumers run these vectors through their implementations in S4-6/S4-8/S4-9; checking envelopes and pins alone is not runtime conformance evidence.

All identities, paths, URLs and file names in fixtures are synthetic. Production hosts, user subjects, credentials and unrelated private files must never be embedded.
